candidates.source_name: 1 Enoch (Ethiopian tradition) / Book of Parables (1 Enoch 37-71)
candidates.draft_body:
1 Enoch (Ethiopian tradition) Book of Parables (1 Enoch 37-71) (c. 100 BC)

'In those days shall the mighty and the kings who possess the earth implore (Him) to grant them a little respite from His angels of punishment to whom they were delivered, that they might fall down and worship before the Lord of Spirits, and confess their sins before Him' — the kings' final repentance attempt. Tewahedo homiletic tradition uses this verse to teach that the time of mercy is BEFORE judgment, not after: the kings ask, but 'there shall be no respite' (63:6). The pastoral application is unflinching.
